run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Only the Loki log source responded in this Run; Kubernetes, Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so pod status, restarts, events, config objects, metrics and traces could not be checked. From payment-api's own logs in namespace app-100a: the single logging pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-mck5b began emitting ERROR lines at 2026-11-20T13:49:24Z (no earlier ERROR line was returned for the 11:00-14:00Z query), reporting 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20 and active_connections 20, plus 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (error_code DB_CONN_001) from PaymentService.processPayment()/DatabasePool.acquire(). Waiting requests reached 46 with wait times up to 26,789 ms. The same period shows a marked rise in its own database work: 'Database query executed' latency was 15-88 ms between 12:30Z and 13:34:45Z and reached 1252 ms at 13:50:55Z, 3106 ms at 14:28:27Z, 4953 ms at 14:30:57Z, 4472 ms at 14:37:32Z and 2355 ms at 14:43:57Z, returning to 12-99 ms from 15:01Z onward; /healthz returned 503 'database unreachable' at 13:57:29Z, 14:01:50Z and 14:44:44Z. The error stream persisted until the last observed ERROR line at 15:13:46Z. Some payments still succeeded during the incident (14:07:40Z 389 ms, 14:09:43Z 323 ms). Supported reading: payment-api exhausted its fixed 20-connection database pool while its database dependency became slow/unreachable; the database entity itself is not visible in any available source, so the origin cannot be named and no root cause object is asserted.

claims.text: Pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-mck5b (service payment-api, namespace app-100a) logged 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 27 and wait_time_ms 17653 at 2026-11-20T13:49:24Z, and continued logging the same message through 14:14:00Z (e.g. waiting_requests 35 / wait_time_ms 6609 at 14:14:00Z).

Within the queried 11:00-14:00Z window the ERROR lines returned for app-100a begin at 13:49:24Z (first 'pool exhausted' line); earlier lines in that window are DEBUG/INFO such as a successful database query of 65 ms at 13:34:45Z.

payment-api also logged 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' with error_code DB_CONN_001 and stack 'at PaymentService.processPayment() ... at DatabasePool.acquire()' at 13:50:55Z, 14:04:41Z and 14:08:14Z.

Connection acquisition pressure deepened later in the incident: at 14:30:57Z the pod logged waiting_requests 46 with wait_time_ms 26398, at 14:32:51Z 25/20933 ms, 14:39:21Z 18/13024 ms and 14:43:57Z 21/26789 ms, all with pool_size 20 and active_connections 20.

The pod's own database query latency rose from a pre-incident range of 15, 18, 30, 61, 65 and 88 ms (timestamps 12:30:17Z-13:34:45Z) to 1252 ms at 13:50:55Z, 3106 ms at 14:28:27Z, 4953 ms at 14:30:57Z, 4472 ms at 14:37:32Z and 2355 ms at 14:43:57Z for the same query 'SELECT * FROM payments WHERE status = ?'.

Database query latency returned to its earlier range after ~15:00Z: 40 ms at 15:01:00Z, 20 ms at 15:05:45Z, 54 ms at 15:07:38Z, 77 ms at 15:14:43Z, 41 ms at 15:15:23Z, and 12-99 ms for all lines returned between 15:33:25Z and 19:59:18Z.

Health checks failed with exact text 'Health check failed - database unreachable' on endpoint /healthz with status_code 503 and response_time_ms 5009 at 13:57:29Z, 9684 at 14:01:50Z and 6354 at 14:44:44Z.

Not every request failed: 'Payment processed successfully' was logged with processing_time_ms 273 (13:00:22Z), 326 (13:18:28Z), 468 (13:31:51Z) before the incident and 389 (14:07:40Z) and 323 (14:09:43Z) during it.

ERROR line counts for app-100a per 30 minutes rose from 1 around 13:50Z to a peak of 13 around 14:20Z and then declined, with the last ERROR sample in the 14:00-20:00Z window at 15:13:46Z (3 per 30 min at that point).

Only one log stream was returned for namespace app-100a in Loki: namespace app-100a, job/service payment-api, pod_name payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-mck5b (25 lines counted in a 45-minute span), and a namespace-wide selector matched no other namespace's stream.

Log-line volume by level shows no large burst at the onset: DEBUG counts per 30 minutes were 7-10 around 13:30-14:30Z versus 4-8 earlier in the same query, and INFO counts were 2-7 (this is emitted log-line volume, not request rate).

The most likely mechanism is that payment-api's fixed 20-connection database pool was starved because its database dependency became slow and intermittently unreachable: query latency rose from <100 ms to 1.2-5 s, connections stayed occupied, waiting requests queued up to 46 with waits up to ~27 s, and /healthz emitted 503 'database unreachable'. The identity, health and own logs of that database (engine, namespace, pod/host) are not visible in any source queried, so the origin of the database problem is unknown.

A configuration-side candidate is that the pool size in effect (20, reported in every exhaustion line) and its timeouts are too small for the concurrent database work of this workload; because Kubernetes and therefore ConfigMaps/Deployment settings were unreadable in this Run, neither the configured value nor any change around 13:45Z could be verified.

A connection leak inside payment-api (connections not released, letting active_connections sit at 20 for ~1.5 h) cannot be excluded; the logs show the same 20/20 saturation from 13:49Z to 14:43Z but carry no connection-release, pool-metric or restart detail that would separate a leak from dependency slowness.

payment-api was not fully down during the window: it kept emitting application logs and completed payments with normal processing times (389 ms at 14:07:40Z, 323 ms at 14:09:43Z) while connection-acquisition failures were being logged.

Rejected as unsupported: that the incident was a pod crash/restart loop or a crash of the payment-api process. The pod emitted a continuous log stream across 13:27Z-15:13Z, some payments succeeded during the failure period, and no startup, listening, shutdown or restart lines were returned by a regex query over 12:00-14:15Z (that query returned only the pool-size error lines). Restart count and termination state could not be read because the Kubernetes source was unavailable.

Check the database dependency that payment-api uses: identify the server/instance, read its saturation, lock, connection-limit and availability signals for 13:40-15:20Z on 2026-11-20, and compare with the recovered period after 15:13Z.

Read the payment-api Deployment and its ConfigMaps for the database pool size (logs report pool_size 20) and acquire timeouts, and check whether the pod template or those settings changed shortly before 13:49Z; a pool sized for the observed concurrency plus a bounded acquire timeout would be the follow-up sizing decision.

Once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable again, confirm the impact and scope with payment error-rate/latency series and with payment operation error spans, and check whether other replicas or callers of payment-api were affected.

gaps: Kubernetes source was unavailable on every attempt (kubernetes_jq_query, kubernetes_tabular_query, fetch_pod_logs all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so pod phase, restart count, last termination reason/exit code, pod conditions, owner chain (Deployment/ReplicaSet) and events for payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-mck5b are unknown.

ConfigMaps, Deployments and Services could not be read, so the configured database pool size/timeouts and any change around 13:45Z are unverified; secrets are unreadable, so any connection-credential/config secret value could not be verified either.

Prometheus was unavailable on every attempt (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error-rate series such as traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name,span_name,status_code}, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{service_name,rpc_service,rpc_method,rpc_grpc_status_code}, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, app_payment_transactions_total and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, plus kube_deployment_status_replicas_available/ready and kube_pod_container_info, are unknown rather than zero.

Jaeger was unavailable (traces_search, traces_list_services/traces_list_operations returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace evidence exists for payment or its callers; whether upstream services saw payment errors is unknown.

The database dependency is unidentified: a Loki query for 'postgres|mysql|pgbouncer|max_connections|too many clients|connection refused' across all jobs in 13:30-14:15Z returned no lines (no_data view), and only the payment-api stream exists in Loki, so the database's own logs and the origin of its slowness/unreachability are unknown.

The onset is only bounded by sampling: first observed ERROR at 13:49:24Z and first observed elevated query latency at 13:50:55Z; nothing in the available sources shows an event at exactly 13:45Z, and log sampling is sparse.
Whether load/request rate increased at the onset is unknown: only emitted log-line counts were observable (no spike), which is not a request-rate measurement.

Persistence after 15:13:46Z is unknown: a query for ERROR lines from 15:13:50Z to 2026-11-21T03:30Z returned no lines (no_data view, an empty result and not proof of absence), and no later recovery or re-recurrence line was observed.
A query for ERROR lines in app-100a between 03:34:13Z and 11:00:00Z returned no lines (no_data view), so the pre-11:00Z state is unchecked rather than proven clean.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment/config change record could be correlated with the 13:45Z onset.
